sourceFacts.fact: Painful or restricted eye movement, proptosis and visual impairment are red flags for orbital cellulitis.
Suspected orbital cellulitis is an emergency requiring urgent assessment, ENT and ophthalmology input and treatment.

expectedLabels: Orbital cellulitis: act on red flags
layoutSpecification: Title 'Orbital cellulitis: act on red flags'. A converging then splitting action diagram. LEFT top: two short directional arrows pushing against an ochre stop-bar beside a small pain-star icon, label 'Painful or limited eye movement'. LEFT bottom: a blurred geometric star and warning flag, label 'Vision change or proptosis'. No eye or face illustration. Two distinct arrows converge at centre: a large hospital-door icon with a simple clock beside it, labelled 'Urgent hospital assessment'. Two arrows leave that hospital to two equal specialist name badges on the RIGHT, top 'ENT', bottom 'Ophthalmology'. These are parallel team inputs, neither must be completed before the other. Keep words short and icons dominant. No wait/watch branch, no doses or scan simulation.
